steps.content: There aren't many people at the cinema on a weekday afternoon, with only six or seven viewers scattered in the vast place. As you and Angell take your seats in the back row with drinks and popcorn, the movie begins.
The film being shown is a recent blockbuster, an epic story adapted from the incidents of Rustfire and Drifter Camp.
The movie starts with a wide shot of a city in ruins, with a massive and intimidating Black Ring floating above it.
Your eyes light up. Pleasantly surprised, you tug at Angell's sleeve.
Wow, look at that Black Ring, it's pretty well done. Looks like they really invested in the CGI for this movie!

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: ...Okay.
Angell glances at you and nods in agreement under your expectant gaze.
The movie's reaching its climax. As one of the witnesses of the story and character inspirations for the movie, you feel like you're revisiting those indelible memories.
The journey was fraught with many hardships and difficulties, but now that it's all in the past, looking back on those times brings a sense of reflection and relief...
Everyone's efforts and perseverance bear meaning, and those sacrifices were not wasted. Darkness will fade, and the hopeful future that once seemed unreachable will eventually come.

Just like what you saw at the farmers' market today, the West District still has a long way to recovery, and various problems remain. But now, people no longer remain silent in the face of oppression and choose to stand up and fight back.
They all truly believe that the era of despair has become the past, and the future of this place will only get better.
As you contemplate, many amusing anecdotes from those tough times also reemerge in your memories.
In the movie, the group of protagonists overcomes obstacles and vanquishes their enemies along the way, making for a thrilling journey to witness.
Hold on, this part is way too exaggerated and idealized...
We were in such a mess back then; everyone was wounded and scattered. It was far from heroic.

In the most critical moments of battle, a character keeps cracking jokes to lighten the mood, drawing not only eye rolls from his companions on the screen but also a few muffled laughs from the audience.
Hahaha, that line does sound like something he would say...

Immersed in the movie, you find it difficult to suppress your comments with someone sitting next to you. As you enthusiastically share your thoughts, you turn and notice Angell looking at you as well.
You smile, a bit embarrassed, and lean in to whisper.
Sorry, you can't focus because I'm talking too much?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: No.
Angell pauses, then adds.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Your commentary... is very interesting.
After saying this, Angell slowly turns her head back to focus on the movie, the light from the screen flickering on her profile.

At the end of the film, a once sunless alley is finally bathed in light, and the laughter of children dispels the dreadful silence. The last shot lingers on a small white flower blooming amidst the dark mire.
The screen fades to black, and the lights in the cinema come on, leaving a long list of credits rolling.
With the soothing end credits music playing, the other viewers slowly exit, leaving just you and Angell in the now empty cinema.
Feeling stiff from sitting for so long, you stretch and turn to Angell with a smile.
What do you think of the movie?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Why do you ask?
After overcoming all the hardships, these people finally live happily and comfortably in the new West District. Sounds pretty good, don't you think?
Angell is smart. She picks up on what you're trying to say, but she shows no reaction and simply replies softly:

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Yeah, but I'm not like them.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: From the very beginning, they had their goals and beliefs. They wanted to bask in the sunlight, and to achieve that goal, they tried their best to break free from the darkness.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: At the same time, there are also people like me on the fringes of the world, who don't see themselves in that picture.
What kind of life do you want?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: The life I have now is good enough. I've already chosen my path.
What made you lose your desire for the sunlight? How did you become who you are today? And why did you make such a choice?
You have many questions, but looking into her tranquil eyes, you suddenly don't know where to start.
There's a moment of silence between you two, Angell is the first to break it.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I've heard that in your world, people like me are considered criminals that need to be captured and shackled, is that true? I'm not too sure.
...Yes, if you don't mind.
Her eyes darken.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: But I won't stay at the MBCC.
I know.
Let's turn this into a commission. I put the shackles on you, and you tell me about your past.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: What do you mean?
We have a bail regulation here. Under this regulation, I have the authority to determine whether a Sinner can be released on bail by evaluating their cases and current condition.
As for the shackles, think of them as a form of security. I won't use them to control you or restrict your freedom.
Angell thinks for a moment, then nods.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Sure.
The crimson glow of the shackles fades, and Angell remains impassive. You pull back your hand.
Alright, let's start from the beginning.
How did you end up in this profession?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: ...I was once just an ordinary Syndican.
Angell falls silent, then begins to share her past with you for the first time.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I was born into a humble family. We led a simple life in a small rented place. We weren't rich, but we didn't have to worry about food and clothing. Although we couldn't afford luxurious meals, my mother would often make sweet red bean soup.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: One night, my parents were caught in a gang shootout on their way home. They were hit by stray bullets and died on the spot, covered in blood. I was still very young at that time.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: With my parents gone and little savings, I couldn't afford the rent. I had no choice but to leave our home and look for ways to make a living.
So you joined the dark web to make a living?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Uh-huh.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: In the early years, I had been everywhere in Syndicate and tried many different jobs. But it turned out I was only good at fighting, killing, and doing dirty work for other people.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: For a long time, I was living hand to mouth, barely scraping by. And one day, I heard about the dark web and how people could make money there, so I registered an account and became a contractor.
As Angell recounts these old stories, her gaze becomes distant.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Back then, I just wanted to earn more money so I wouldn't starve to death, that was it.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: But as I got more jobs, I also made more enemies. To stay alive, I had to stay vigilant at all times.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I couldn't leave my house, nor stay in the same place for more than two months. My blade was always within arm's reach. The curtains in my house had to stay drawn at all times, or the windows had to be painted black...

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: It was during that time that I slowly lost my sense of taste, forgot what an ordinary life looked like, how to find joy in beautiful things, and began eating merely to survive.
What kind of life was that? The safe house ensured her safety, but it also became her prison.
You can't help feeling sorry for her.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: When I was in the safe house, I occasionally reminisced about the days when I lived with my family, but those memories felt so distant, like they belonged to a past life.
So you thought about the past... have you tried going back to living a normal life?
Angell smiles, her voice carrying a hint of resignation.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I tried, but you can see how that turned out.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: After landing a few big jobs, I was able to establish myself on the dark web. Over time, I earned enough to buy a new identity and start a new life.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: And I did that. I went to a new place with good security and privacy.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I stopped going on the dark web. I still had to be constantly aware of my surroundings and hide my identity, but I could occasionally get out of the house.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: There was a small restaurant near my place. They had red bean soup, so I would sometimes go there to get some.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I thought I could live out the rest of my life quietly like that, but it only lasted for three months or so.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Some people from the dark web found me. They thought that red bean soup place was one of my hideouts, so they killed the owner and his family, ruined that beautiful restaurant.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: The only survivors were a tank of red goldfish.
And you brought them back with you? Are they the same ones you keep in the safe house?
Angell shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: That was many years ago. Those goldfish all died, but since then I have been keeping a tank of goldfish.
Her tone remains flat, but your heart feels heavy.
Sorry for bringing up these sad memories again. It must have been difficult for you.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Rather than sad, "liberated" might be a better word to describe what I felt.
Liberated?
You look up in surprise, confused.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: During the days of living on the edge, I longed for the peace I once had, and each night I dreamed of wonderful things.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: But during that seemingly peaceful time, I was always thinking about how to hide my identity and flee my past. My dreams were consumed by my life on the dark web as well.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: After that incident, I realized that I had become a shark accustomed to the deep waters.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I can't respond to kindness from others, fearing I might harm innocent people. I'm too sensitive to malice and hostility due to my Mania; I might overreact instinctively and accidentally hurt someone.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: But now, none of that really matters anymore.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Because I've finally fully adapted to the dark web and I can live well here. The dark side of the city always exists, but there's no need to worry or flee because I can survive on this side. The darkness is no longer my enemy; it has become my "haven."

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: This is my past.
Angell recounts her past calmly, like an unfeeling onlooker. Her tone and expression reveal no sadness or regret.
What should you say to her?
Stunned by her story, you're at a loss for words, even though you're usually so eloquent.
Should you tell her you understand her, that the past is behind her, and she should keep hope alive? Or maybe ask her to trust you and step into the sunlight together?
None of them feels right, because she doesn't need comfort or encouragement.
You still want to convince her, yet after learning about the blood and tears she endured in the past, everything you say feels weak and inadequate.
Angell watches you quietly, as if she has already seen through you.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: ...${PlayerName}.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I know you're used to saving and helping people. When you see someone stuck and suffering in the abyss, you try desperately to pull them out like it's your responsibility.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: But not everyone needs or yearns to be saved. You can't save everyone.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I know you've more than once asked me to go back with you into the sunlight.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: You can try to persuade me, or show me the beauty of your world again and again, my answer still remains the same.
Having said that, Angell quietly waits for your reply. You see a hint of helplessness in her eyes, but also her determination.
The screen has turned pitch-black, seems like the movie's credits have already ended at some point. With no music in the background, all you can hear is your breathing in the silent cinema.
...I see.
After a long while, you let out a sigh and nod.
I'm still trying and asking these questions only because we've never had the chance to truly talk about it.
I knew how you might react, but I still had a glimpse of hope that maybe I could persuade you.
But now that you've told me how you feel about this, I won't insist.
You're right, perhaps I've been too caught up in the so-called "savior" role, but I hope you will understand and forgive me for being stubborn and selfish.

I've always believed no one is meant to live in the shadows, and that deep down, everyone yearns for the warmth of the sun. I thought you didn't want to come with me because you don't trust this side of the world.
I thought that if I tried harder and proved myself worthy of your trust, I could ease your worries and pull you out of the mire.
But now it seems, that's not the case.
I was wrong.
You pause, then look back at Angell, flashing a broad smile.
I respect your decision. I won't impose my own beliefs on you anymore.
Since you can't accept this kind of life, I won't go against your wishes and force you to stay.
After finishing your sentence, you get up from your seat.
Let's go, the movie has ended for a while now.
